items.question: What binds the speaker to the supreme goddess?
premises: The speaker addresses the supreme goddess directly.
The speaker claims to be bound.
Affection and devotion are the binding forces.
items.inference: The speaker is bound to the supreme goddess by affection and devotion.
items.plain_english: O supreme goddess, I am bound by your affection and devotion.

items.question: Which preparatory practices should the practitioner perform next?
premises: Breath-control is prescribed as a practice.
A six-limbed ritual is prescribed.

items.inference: The practitioner should then perform breath-control and the six-limbed ritual by ritual power.

items.plain_english: Then one should perform breath-control and the six-limbed rite by means of māyā.

items.question: What daily offering must be given to the goddess?

The offering involves remnant red substance.

items.plain_english: One should give her an offering with the remnant red substance day after day.

rows.grounds: instrument of worship; form as given

items.question: By what means should the goddess be worshipped daily?
premises: Worship is enjoined as a daily act.
Body, mind, and speech are specified as means.
The worship is to be performed every day.
items.inference: One should worship her daily with body, mind, and speech.
items.plain_english: And one should worship her day after day with body, mind, and speech.

items.question: How long and under what condition should the mantra be recited?
premises: Mantra recitation is prescribed.
A delightful offering must be given beforehand.
The recitation continues until midnight.
items.inference: After giving a delightful offering, one should recite the mantra until midnight.
items.plain_english: Having given a delightful offering, one should recite the mantra until midnight.

items.question: What should the best practitioner do upon seeing the goddess?
premises: The best practitioner may see the goddess.
Seeing her prompts a ritual response.
An offering and related items are to be given.
items.inference: Upon seeing her, the best practitioner should then give the offering and so forth.
items.plain_english: Then, having seen her, the best practitioner should also give the offering and so forth.

items.question: What happens after the goddess leaves garments and ornaments behind?
premises: Garments, ornaments, and related items are abandoned.
The goddess is the agent of departure.
She returns to her own abode.
items.inference: After abandoning garments, ornaments, and so forth, she goes to her own abode.
items.plain_english: Having left behind garments, ornaments, and so forth, she goes to her own abode.

items.question: Whom must the wise practitioner worship after abandoning his own wife?
premises: The wise practitioner is instructed to abandon his own wife.
Worship of another female figure is enjoined.
The instruction is directed to a discerning practitioner.
items.inference: The wise practitioner, having abandoned his own wife, should worship her.
uncertainties: This is a transgressive ritual injunction requiring careful contextual interpretation
items.plain_english: Having abandoned his own wife, the wise one should worship her.

rows.grounds: epithet of the mantra or goddess

items.question: What benefit does the great mantra of the fire's wife bring practitioners?
premises: The wife of fire is identified as a great mantra.
Practitioners are the recipients of its effect.
The mantra brings happiness.
items.inference: The great mantra, the wife of fire, brings happiness to practitioners.
uncertainties: vahneḥ bhāryā may refer to Svāhā or a specific goddess
items.plain_english: The great mantra, the wife of fire, brings happiness to practitioners.

items.question: What result follows meditating and reciting the mantra at midnight?
premises: Meditation and mantra recitation are prescribed.
The practice is performed in the prescribed manner.
Midnight is the specified time of manifestation.
items.inference: Thus meditating and reciting the mantra, she comes at midnight.
items.plain_english: Thus, having meditated and recited the mantra, she comes at midnight.

items.question: How should the practitioner receive the goddess upon her arrival?
premises: The goddess arrives at the appointed time.
She is to be received with the attitude toward a woman.
Foot-water and related honors are to be offered.
items.inference: Then, with the attitude toward a woman, one should offer her foot-water and so forth.
items.plain_english: Then, with the attitude due to a woman, one should offer her foot-water and so forth.

items.question: In what manner should the practitioner attend to the goddess?
premises: Food and other offerings are to be provided.
Sexual enjoyment is included in the service.
The practitioner should act like a husband.
items.inference: One should always attend to her like a husband with food and sexual enjoyment.
uncertainties: This is a transgressive ritual injunction requiring careful contextual interpretation
items.plain_english: One should always attend to her like a husband, with food and with sexual enjoyment.

items.question: What attainment results from performing this practice every day?
premises: The prescribed practice is performed daily.
A result is promised to the practitioner.
The attainment takes the form of desire.
items.inference: By practicing thus every day, he may attain success in the form of desire.
uncertainties: kāma-rūpataḥ may mean according to desire or in the form of Kāma
items.plain_english: Thus, by practicing every day, he may attain success in the form of desire.

items.question: How many times must the fire-wife mantra be recited daily?
premises: The mantra of the fire's wife is specified.
A specific count of recitations is prescribed.
The recitation is to be done every day.
items.inference: One should recite the mantra of the fire's wife eight thousand times every day.
uncertainties: aṣṭa+sahastryaṃ form is unusual; interpreted as eight thousand
items.plain_english: One should recite the mantra of the fire's wife eight thousand times day after day.

items.question: Under what condition does the goddess certainly come at midnight?
premises: The goddess recognizes the practitioner.
The practitioner must be firm and eminent.
Midnight is the time of her coming.
items.inference: Knowing the best practitioner to be firm, she certainly comes at midnight.
items.plain_english: Knowing the best practitioner to be firm, she certainly comes at midnight.

items.question: How does the very satisfied goddess please the best practitioner?
premises: The goddess becomes very satisfied.
She acts to please the best practitioner.
Sexual enjoyments are the means.
items.inference: Being very satisfied, she should please the best practitioner with sexual enjoyments.
items.plain_english: Very satisfied, she pleases the best practitioner with sexual enjoyments.

rows.grounds: goddess as object; form as given

items.question: What consequence follows if the practitioner does not worship her exclusively?
premises: Abandoning one's wife and worshipping her is enjoined.
An alternative course of action is considered.

items.inference: Having abandoned his wife he should worship her; otherwise he certainly perishes.
uncertainties: āñca is a nonstandard form for tāñca/enām ca
items.plain_english: Having abandoned his wife, he should worship her; otherwise he certainly perishes.

items.question: Why does the goddess go to the practitioner's abode?
premises: The goddess perceives welfare everywhere.
This perception precedes her movement.
She goes to the practitioner's abode.
items.inference: Knowing welfare everywhere, she goes to the practitioner's abode.
items.plain_english: Knowing welfare everywhere, she goes to the practitioner's abode.

items.question: What ongoing exclusive devotion is required of the best practitioner?
premises: The best practitioner is addressed directly.
Abandoning one's wife is required.
Continuous worship of her is enjoined.
items.inference: O beloved, the best practitioner, having abandoned his wife, should always worship her.

items.plain_english: O beloved, having abandoned his wife, the best practitioner should always worship her.

items.question: Which accomplished forms of knowledge are identified to the beloved?
premises: A knowledge is described as accomplished.
Two names are given for this knowledge.
The beloved is addressed directly.
items.inference: O beloved, know the accomplished knowledge called Balā and Atibalā.
items.plain_english: O beloved, know the accomplished knowledge called Balā and Atibalā.

items.question: How must the great knowledge be treated after being named?
premises: The knowledge is called a great knowledge.
A directive regarding its treatment is given.
Concealment must be done with effort.
items.inference: This, called the great knowledge, must be carefully concealed.
items.plain_english: This, called the great knowledge, must be concealed with effort.

items.question: With what mantra and mental state should all rites be performed?
premises: All ritual actions are to be performed.
The root mantra is the prescribed instrument.
The practitioner must be well concentrated.

items.plain_english: And, being well concentrated, one should do everything with the root mantra.

items.question: How many daily mantra recitations are prescribed after meditation?
premises: Meditation precedes recitation.
The mantra is to be recited.
A thousand recitations are prescribed daily.
items.inference: Thus having meditated, one should recite the mantra a thousand times every day.
items.plain_english: Thus, having meditated, one should recite the mantra a thousand times day after day.

items.question: What offerings should the wise practitioner always give to her?
premises: The wise practitioner is the agent.
Fragrance, sandalwood, and betel are specified.
These offerings are to be given always.
items.inference: The wise one should always give her fragrance, sandalwood, and betel.
items.plain_english: The wise one should always give her fragrance, sandalwood, and betel.
